steps.body: Standing things compare by the same rule turned upright: same floor as the start line, and the top that reaches higher is TALLER.
steps.narration: Standing things compare by the same rule turned upright: same floor as the start line, and the top that reaches higher is TALLER.

widget.prompt: Measure the tower. Align zero with its start, then place 5 one-unit blocks with no gaps or overlaps.
widget.successFeedback: 5 equal blocks cover the tower exactly — same start, no gaps, no overlaps: that count names its length in blocks.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Use same-size blocks so every count names the same unit.

predict.prompt: Two towers on the same floor. The taller one is the one that…
predict.reveal: Tallness is vertical reach from the shared floor; width is a different attribute altogether.

cml.actionGoal: Compare fairly — same start line, level seesaw, one sorting rule — for kmd taller shorter.
invariants: Fair comparison has fixed rules: lengths compare from one same start line, weights compare by which pan sinks, and sorted groups compare by their counts — the anchors for kmd taller shorter.
misconceptions: Judging length before aligning starts, reading size as weight, or comparing groups by how much space they fill instead of their counts.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the starts were not lined up, could the far ends still settle which is longer?

widget.prompt: Compare the three towers from one start line and tap the tallest.

items.label: left tower
items.feedback: The left one measures 5 cubes — shorter than 7. Count the unit ticks, not the look.

items.label: right tower
items.feedback: The right one measures 3 cubes — shorter than 7. Count the unit ticks, not the look.

widget.missFeedback: From one start line the far end decides: the tallest reaches 7 cubes.
widget.successFeedback: Right — same start line, so the farther end IS the tallest.

widget.prompt: A giraffe and a lamppost stand side by side on level ground, feet lined up. The giraffe's head reaches higher. Which is taller?

options.label: The lamppost — poles are always taller than animals
options.feedback: Height is not decided by category; only the compared tops from a lined-up bottom decide.

options.label: You cannot tell without a ruler
options.feedback: Lined-up bottoms already answer it — the higher top is taller, no ruler needed.

options.label: They must be the same height
options.feedback: Nothing forces equal height; the higher top from the same ground line settles it.

options.label: The giraffe — its top reaches higher
options.feedback: Correct — with both feet on the same ground line, the higher top is the taller one.
